name: CUTDOWN
summary: Punch in/out on a folder of footage and let the lane render the cuts.

provider._note: This app is a CLIENT of that provider. Installing the surface alone gets you an HTML file that 502s — the field rigs-to-apps v1 had no slot for, which is why media-manager was listed there and was not installable.

companions.label: cut lane
companions._note: The renderer the write verbs enqueue for. Without it stabilize and cut-retry accept work nothing performs — declared so it starts WITH the provider rather than being remembered.

provider._serves_note: BYTE-route prefixes. A backend is not only its /api/ verbs — these were undeclared, so the front proxied only /api/* and clips listed but would not play.
provider._supplies_note: Binaries this provider SHIPS (ffmpeg-static/ffprobe-static), so the host does not need them. requires.binaries still declares the NEED — that stays legible and true; this says who satisfies it. Without the distinction the installer refuses a working install on any box without a system ffmpeg, which is most of them.

requires._filters_note: REQUIRED vs PREFERRED, and the split is the point. scale/concat are load-bearing: no cut renders without them. drawtext only writes the LABEL on a placeholder slate, and the assembler now renders an unlabelled slate and reports the degradation instead of failing the export. So drawtext must NOT block an install — the Linux ffmpeg-static build (7.0.2) lacks it while the macOS one (6.0) has it, and losing a caption on an unshot beat is not worth refusing a working studio.
